implementation_notes: C absorbs the classic two-class Essence structure into its dominant API idiom: the target type is declared in the header as an opaque handle (typedef struct contract *contract_t) with the struct definition hidden in the .c file, so no client can instantiate it directly and the validating factory function contract_create() is the only door - the create function's parameters (or a const config struct, the my_module_config_t style) play the Essence role, its NULL return plays validateParameters(), and contract_destroy() is the mandatory counterpart. Validation of all compulsory properties (non-NULL, non-empty customer/supplier, sane date range) runs BEFORE any allocation, so an invalid call never produces even a half-built object; strdup() copies the compulsory strings so the object is self-contained and immutable-by-convention after creation. A two-phase *_init-on-caller-storage variant exists for allocation-free embedded code, but it reopens a window in which the object exists yet is invalid, so the single validating create remains the realization of the Always-Valid invariant.
pitfalls: No compiler-enforced constructor privacy: the invariant holds only while the struct definition stays in the .c file; once it leaks into a header, clients can stack-allocate or zero a raw struct and bypass every check - the opaque definition is load-bearing, not decorative.

Partial-failure cleanup is manual: when the second strdup() fails, the first copy leaks unless the failure path calls the destructor - C has no RAII unwind, so every early return after an allocation needs its own cleanup.

Never store caller string pointers: a compulsory property kept as the caller's const char * dangles the moment the caller's buffer dies or is mutated; strdup() (POSIX.1-2008) the value or document shallow ownership explicitly.

Ignore the NULL return and the crash is immediate: unlike exceptions, nothing forces the check, so treat contract_create() == NULL as part of the API contract and never dereference before testing - a 'created but unvalidated' struct read is undefined behavior, since heap objects in C start with indeterminate contents.

Avoid two-phase *_init APIs for compulsory properties: between allocation and a successful _init() the object exists in an invalid state, which is exactly what the pattern forbids; reserve _init/_terminate for static-storage allocation-free contexts where create cannot be used.
A shared, mutable config-struct Essence shared across threads is a data race: keep the Essence inputs (parameters or a const config struct) call-local, or copy them before validation.
